question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the Official Languages of the Indian Union? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Part XX
Part XV
Part XVII
Part XVI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part XVII

Explanation:
Part XVII of the Indian Constitution (Articles 343 to 351) deals with the official languages of the Union. Article 343 declares Hindi as the official language, while Article 345 allows states to adopt their own official languages. Articles 346 and 347 govern the language of communication between the Union and states. Article 348 specifies the language to be used in the Supreme Court and High Courts. Article 351 directs the promotion of Hindi. Part XV deals with elections, Part XVI with special provisions for certain classes, and Part XX with amendments. Thus, Part XVII is correct.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which part of the Constitution deals with official languages? → Part XVII
☛ Which articles relate to official language? → 343-351
☛ Which article declares Hindi as official language? → Article 343
☛ Which article deals with language of High Courts? → Article 348
☛ Which article directs development of Hindi? → Article 351
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा भाग, भारतीय संघ की राजभाषाओं से संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 3)

भाग XV
भाग XVII
भाग XVI
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग XVII

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग XVII (अनुच्छेद 343 से 351) संघ की राजभाषाओं से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 343 में हिंदी को राजभाषा घोषित किया गया है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 345 राज्यों को अपनी राजभाषा निर्धारित करने की अनुमति देता है। अनुच्छेद 346 और 347 संघ और राज्यों के बीच संचार की भाषा से संबंधित हैं। अनुच्छेद 348 उच्च न्यायालयों में प्रयोग की जाने वाली भाषा को परिभाषित करता है। अनुच्छेद 351 हिंदी के विकास का निर्देश देता है। भाग XV चुनावों से, भाग XVI विशेष वर्गों से, और भाग XX संशोधनों से संबंधित है।

question: Which amendment to the Indian constitution provided a special status to the Union Territory of Delhi, and redesignated it the National Capital Territory of Delhi? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 69th Constitutional Amendment
68th Constitutional Amendment
70th Constitutional Amendment
71st Constitutional Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 69th Constitutional Amendment

Explanation:
The 69th Constitutional Amendment (1991) granted special status to Delhi, redesignating it as the National Capital Territory. It inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB, providing for a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister. However, subjects like police, land, and public order remained under central control. This amendment was based on the recommendations of the Shah, Sitaram, and Sapru Commissions. Prior to this, Delhi was a regular Union Territory administered by the Centre through a Lieutenant Governor. The 69th Amendment gave Delhi partial statehood, making it distinct from other Union Territories.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Amendment that gave Delhi the status of National Capital Territory → 69th Amendment (1991)
☛ Articles inserted by the 69th Amendment → 239AA and 239AB
☛ Maximum number of members in Delhi Legislative Assembly → 70
☛ Subjects under central control in Delhi → Police, land, and public order
☛ Date of enforcement of the 69th Amendment → 1 February 1992

question:
According to Article 171 of the Constitution of India, the total membership of a State’s Legislative Council shall not surpass which of the following proportions of the total members of the State Legislative Assembly?
(RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: One-third
One-fourth
One-half
Two-thirds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is One-third

Explanation:
According to Article 171, the total membership of a State's Legislative Council shall not exceed one-third of the total membership of the State Legislative Assembly. This provision applies to states with bicameral legislatures, such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana. Members of the Legislative Council are elected from various constituencies (local bodies, teachers, graduates, Legislative Assembly members, and nominated by the Governor). It is a permanent house that cannot be dissolved fully. This ratio ensures that the Legislative Council remains smaller than the Assembly, maintaining the supremacy of the Assembly.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Creation of Legislative Council → Under Articles 169 and 171
☛ Maximum membership of Legislative Council → Not more than one-third of Assembly membership
☛ Term of Legislative Council members → 6 years, with one-third retiring every two years
☛ Minimum membership of Legislative Council → 40 members
☛ Correct ratio as per Article 171(3) → One-third
question_hi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 171 के अनुसार, किसी राज्य की विधान परिषद की कुल सदस्यता, राज्य विधान सभा के कुल सदस्यों के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुपात से अधिक नहीं होगी? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 1)

question: In accordance with Article 84 of the Constitution of India, which of the following is the minimum age a person must meet to qualify for membership of the House of the People? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Twenty-one years
Twenty-five years
Thirty years
Eighteen years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Twenty-five years

Explanation:
Article 84 of the Constitution of India lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament. For the House of the People (Lok Sabha), a person must be at least twenty-five years of age. In contrast, for the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), the minimum age is thirty years. This age requirement ensures that candidates have sufficient maturity and experience to effectively represent the people. The Constitution also requires that the person be a citizen of India and meet any additional qualifications prescribed by Parliament. Other options: 21 years (minimum for state legislative assemblies), 30 years (for Rajya Sabha), and 18 years (voting age).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Minimum age for Lok Sabha membership → 25 years
☛ Minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership → 30 years
☛ Minimum age for State Legislative Assembly membership → 21 years
☛ Minimum voting age in India → 18 years
☛ Other conditions under Article 84 → Citizen of India and fulfill other qualifications prescribed by Parliament

question: In accordance with Article 239AA of the Constitution of India, after the enforcement of the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union Territory of Delhi is designated by which of the following titles? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Administrative Capital of India
National Capital Region of Delhi
Union State of Delhi
National Capital Territory of Delhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Capital Territory of Delhi

Explanation:
Article 239AA of the Indian Constitution grants Delhi the special status of National Capital Territory (NCT). The 69th Amendment Act (1991) provided Delhi with a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers to legislate on certain matters. However, the central government retains control through President's rule and the Ministry of Home Affairs. Other options are incorrect: Administrative Capital of India is not a constitutional title; NCR is a planning region covering Delhi and surrounding areas; Union State of Delhi does not exist.

question: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is it stated that Union Territories are to be administered by the President, who may appoint an administrator to oversee them? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Article 241
Article 239
Article 242
Article 240
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239

Explanation:
Article 239 of the Indian Constitution states that every Union Territory shall be administered by the President acting through an administrator appointed by him. This article is part of Part VIII of the Constitution, which deals with Union Territories. The President may appoint an administrator for each Union Territory, who acts as his representative. Additionally, Article 239 gives the President the power to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of the Union Territories. Notably, Article 240 provides special regulation-making powers for certain Union Territories, while Article 241 relates to High Courts. Thus, the core provision regarding the administration of Union Territories is enshrined in Article 239.

☛ Part of Constitution covering Union Territories → Part VIII

question: What condition must be fulfilled by a person born outside India after December 3, 2004, to be considered an Indian citizen by descent? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 2)

They must reside in India for at least 5 years.
They must renounce any other nationality.

solution:

Explanation:
According to Article 8 of the Indian Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955, for a person born outside India after December 3, 2004, to be considered an Indian citizen by descent, it is necessary that both parents are Indian citizens. This provision was introduced by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003. Previously, if either parent was an Indian citizen, the child could claim citizenship by descent, but after 2004, the condition was tightened. There is no requirement of residency in India or renunciation of any other nationality for this category.

question: A person born in India between 26 January 1950 and 1 July 1987 is automatically considered a citizen of India by: (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: descent
naturalisation
registration
birth
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is birth

Explanation:
Under the Indian Constitution, any person born in India between 26 January 1950 and 1 July 1987 was automatically considered a citizen of India by birth. This provision is outlined in Section 3 of the Citizenship Act, 1955. During this period, individuals born in India did not require any additional process to acquire citizenship. After 1 July 1987, it became mandatory that at least one parent must be an Indian citizen for a person born in India to be a citizen by birth. Other modes of acquiring citizenship include descent (for those born outside India to Indian parents), naturalisation (for foreigners), and registration (for persons of Indian origin abroad). However, for the specific period mentioned, 'birth' is the correct basis.

question: The Right to Property was removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution and added to _____. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Part XII
Part X
Part XIII
Part XI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part XII

Explanation:
The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31 of Part III of the Indian Constitution. However, the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed it from Part III and added it as Article 300A under Part XII, making it a constitutional right rather than a fundamental right. This amendment was introduced to facilitate land reforms and equitable distribution of resources. Now, no person can be deprived of their property except by the authority of law. Being a constitutional right, its violation does not allow direct petition to the Supreme Court under Article 32; instead, one must approach the High Court under Article 226. The amendment came into effect on 20 June 1979.

☛ Under which Article is Right to Property now? → Article 300A
☛ Under which Part is Right to Property now? → Part XII
☛ What type of right is Right to Property now? → Constitutional right
☛ When was 44th Amendment enacted? → 20 June 1979

question: The Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019, provides citizenship to individuals belonging to which communities if they entered India before 31st December 2014 from Pakistan or Afghanistan or Bangladesh? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Sikh, Christian, Hindu, Jain only
Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian
Muslim, Christian, Parsi, Sikh
Hindu, Muslim, Jain, Parsi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian

Explanation:
The Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 (CAA) grants Indian citizenship to immigrants who entered India from Pakistan, Afghanistan, or Bangladesh before 31st December 2014 and belong to the Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, or Christian communities. This Act amends the Citizenship Act, 1955 and reduces the residency requirement for naturalization from 11 years to 5 years for these communities. The Muslim community is excluded from the Act on the grounds that these countries are Muslim-majority and hence Muslims there do not face religious persecution. The Act has been a subject of debate regarding its conformity with the Assam Accord and the right to equality under Article 14.

Later, the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted under Article 11 to provide for acquisition and termination of citizenship after commencement.

question: What is the constitutional consequence if the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion against the ruling government? (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is removed by the President
The government may continue without any change
Only the Prime Minister must submit resignation
The Council of Ministers is obligated to step down
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Council of Ministers is obligated to step down

Explanation:
According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. When the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, it signifies that the government has lost the confidence of the lower house. Under constitutional convention and Article 75, the entire Council of Ministers must resign. The resignation of only the Prime Minister is insufficient because the principle of collective responsibility applies. The President then may explore alternative arrangements, such as inviting another party to form a government or dissolving the Lok Sabha. This process is a fundamental aspect of parliamentary democracy.

question: When a law passed by a State Legislature clashes with a Parliamentary law on a Concurrent List subject, what is the legal outcome? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: The matter is settled through a ruling by the Supreme Court
The state legislation automatically overrides the central law
The central law overrides the state law unless the state law has Presidential assent
The Parliament is obligated to annul the state law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The central law overrides the state law unless the state law has Presidential assent

Explanation:
Under the Indian Constitution, both the Centre and states can legislate on subjects in the Concurrent List. When a state law clashes with a central law on a concurrent subject, the central law prevails generally. However, if the state law has received Presidential assent, it can operate in that state and override the central law. This provision is enshrined in Article 254 of the Constitution. Thus, unless the state law obtains Presidential assent, the central law remains supreme. Other options are incorrect because the matter does not always go to the Supreme Court, the state law does not automatically override, and Parliament is not obligated to annul the state law.

☛ When can Parliament legislate on a State List subject? → By a Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest

question: Which of these Union Territories has a legislative assembly and council of ministers? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Daman and Diu
Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Puducherry
Dadra and Nagar Haveli
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Puducherry

Explanation:
Among the Union Territories of India, only Puducherry and Delhi have a legislative assembly and council of ministers. Puducherry is provided with a legislative assembly and council of ministers under Article 239A of the Constitution. Its legislative assembly has 30 members, and the Chief Minister is its head. Other Union Territories such as Daman and Diu, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli do not have a legislative assembly; they are directly administered by the central government. The system of legislative assembly and council of ministers in Puducherry makes it unique.
